subject: biology
title: Reproduction in Plants
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: An unfertilised female gametophyte of an angiosperm has —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: The correct order of layers of a young anther from the outer to the inner side is —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Self-pollination is observed in pea plants as their —
options: stamens and pistils develop at the same time (synchronous) in closed flowers
stamens and pistils develop at different times
stamens and pistils are found in different plants
male and female sex organs are found in different flowers
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Double fertilisation is a characteristic of —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The ploidy of the primary endosperm nucleus is —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Pollination by water is called —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The cells that guide the pollen tube towards the egg are the —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The innermost wall layer of the anther that nourishes pollen grains is the —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Epigeal germination is seen in —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Parthenocarpic fruits are —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The outer wall of the pollen grain is made of —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The part of the ovule that forms the seed coat is the —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Low temperature treatment which promotes early flowering is —
questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks (any two): (a) ______ and ______ are devices that ensure self-pollination. (b) ______ and ______ are adaptations to promote cross-pollination.
questions.answer: (a) Cleistogamy and homogamy. (b) Dichogamy and self-sterility (also unisexuality).

questions.q: Label the parts of the androecium and gynoecium (any one).
questions.answer: Androecium: anther (with pollen sacs), connective and filament. Gynoecium: stigma, style and ovary (with ovules).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Yeast reproduces by the ______ method.
questions.answer: budding.

questions.q: Name the three types of sexual reproduction in Chlamydomonas.
questions.answer: Isogamy, anisogamy and oogamy.

questions.q: Match: (a) Bryophyllum (b) Agave (c) Ginger with (i) bulbil (ii) leaf buds (iii) rhizome.
State true or false: (a) The pollen grain is the male gamete. (b) Apomixis involves no fertilisation.
questions.answer: (a) False – it is the male gametophyte. (b) True.

questions.q: Name the cells of the egg apparatus and of the chalazal end.
questions.answer: Egg cell and two synergids; three antipodal cells.

questions.q: Name the artificial methods of vegetative propagation with one example each.
questions.answer: Cutting (rose), layering (jasmine), grafting (mango) and tissue culture (orchids).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Differentiate between asexual and sexual reproduction (two points).
questions.answer: Asexual involves a single parent without fusion of gametes and the offspring are identical; sexual involves two gametes and the offspring show variation.

questions.q: What is parthenocarpy? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Development of fruit without fertilisation, giving seedless fruits; e.g. banana and grapes.

questions.q: What is polyembryony? Name its two types.
questions.answer: More than one embryo in a seed: adventive (from other cells of the embryo sac) and cleavage (from division of the zygote).

questions.q: What is vernalisation?
questions.answer: Low temperature treatment that stimulates early flowering in some plants.

questions.q: List any four advantages of vegetative propagation.
questions.answer: It is rapid and cheap, the offspring are identical to the parent, food storage organs allow perennation and it ensures survival of seedless varieties.

questions.q: Write the functions of synergids and antipodal cells.
questions.answer: Synergids guide the pollen tube to the egg; antipodals degenerate and provide nutrition to the young embryo.

questions.q: Differentiate between epigeal and hypogeal germination (one example each).
questions.answer: In epigeal the cotyledons come above the ground (castor); in hypogeal they stay underground (maize).

questions.q: What is apomixis?
questions.answer: Production of seeds without fertilisation from a diploid cell of the ovule (dandelion).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Briefly explain double fertilisation in an angiosperm. Mention the end products formed by this process.
questions.answer: The pollen tube releases two sperms into the embryo sac; one fuses with the egg (syngamy) to give the diploid zygote and the other fuses with the diploid secondary nucleus (triple fusion) to give the triploid primary endosperm nucleus. End products: embryo and endosperm.

questions.q: Describe the structure of the mature embryo sac.
questions.answer: It has seven cells and eight nuclei: an egg apparatus (egg and two synergids) at the micropylar end, three antipodal cells at the chalazal end and a large central cell with two polar nuclei that fuse to form the secondary nucleus.

questions.q: Write the adaptations of wind-pollinated flowers.
questions.answer: Small, colourless, odourless flowers; large numbers of light or winged pollen; large, hairy and protruding stigmas.

questions.q: Explain the structure of the maize grain.
questions.answer: It has a pericarp fused with the seed coat, an endosperm with a protein-rich aleurone layer and a single large cotyledon (scutellum), with the embryonal axis lying lateral to it.

questions.q: Explain the method of micropropagation.
questions.answer: A small piece of plant tissue is cultured in a sterile nutrient medium; it forms a callus, which on a hormone medium forms plantlets; these are transplanted; an indefinite number of identical plants can be produced.

questions.q: Differentiate between self-pollination and cross-pollination.
questions.answer: Self-pollination is the transfer to the stigma of the same flower or plant (pea); cross-pollination is the transfer to a flower of another plant (palm, maize), producing variation.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the development of the male gametophyte (pollen grain) in angiosperms.
questions.answer: The anther has four microsporangia with tapetum; microspore mother cells divide by meiosis into four microspores (tetrad); each forms a pollen grain with exine and intine; its nucleus divides into a vegetative and a generative cell, which gives two male gametes.

questions.q: Describe the development of the female gametophyte (embryo sac).
questions.answer: A megaspore mother cell in the nucellus divides by meiosis into four megaspores; three degenerate; the functional megaspore divides three times to give eight nuclei, which form the egg apparatus, antipodals and the central cell with polar nuclei.

questions.q: Explain the types of pollination and the characteristics of wind- and insect-pollinated flowers.
questions.answer: Self and cross pollination; wind pollinated: small, scentless flowers, light pollen, large stigma; insect pollinated: large, coloured, scented flowers with nectar and sticky pollen.

questions.q: Describe the reproduction of Chlamydomonas.
questions.answer: Asexual by zoospores, aplanospores and hypnospores; sexual by isogamy, anisogamy and oogamy, with a diploid zygote that undergoes meiosis to produce four haploid zoospores.

questions.q: Describe the post-fertilisation changes in a flower.
questions.answer: Endosperm formed from the primary endosperm nucleus; embryo from the zygote with suspensor; integuments form the seed coat; the ovule becomes the seed and the ovary becomes the fruit; fruit ripening.

questions.q: Explain the artificial methods of vegetative propagation.
questions.answer: Cuttings, layering and aerial layering, grafting (stock and scion) and tissue culture, with examples and advantages.
